correctness.rationale: Newton–Schulz gives the exact residual recurrence E_{k+1}=E_k^2. In 2x2, unitary Schur form reduces the Frobenius comparison to |a|^4+|b|^4+|z|^2|a+b|^2 versus |a|^2+|b|^2+|z|^2. Spectral radius at most 1/2 makes every term nonexpansive, while the Jordan family with repeated eigenvalue r>1/2 becomes expansive for sufficiently large off-diagonal entry. In 3x3, the two-edge nilpotent shift has E_0^2 with one entry M^2, giving exact Frobenius amplification M/sqrt(2), spectral amplification M, and E_0^4=0. Taking A=I and X_0=I-E_0 realizes the residual sequence as an actual inverse iteration. The packaged exact-rational checker replays representative identities.

value.rationale: Newton–Schulz is commonly justified by residual squaring and the spectral-radius convergence condition, while residual norms are natural diagnostics for approximate inverses. The theorem shows exactly how far asymptotic spectral convergence is from stepwise residual safety: dimension two has a sharp universal spectral-radius ceiling, but dimension three permits arbitrarily large residual deterioration even at zero spectral radius and for a condition-one target, immediately followed by exact termination. The minimal-dimension and exact-termination features make this more informative than a generic nonnormal-transient example.
